title: What Is an Echo? 🔊 Kids Science
description:
An echo is sound bouncing back to you! Leo asks, Dad explains sound waves, echoes and how bats use them, in under a minute.

tags: what is an echo for kids

lines.text: An echo is a sound that bounces back to you. Like when you shout 'Hello!' near a big cliff, and you hear 'hello' again.
It can! Sound travels through the air in invisible waves, a bit like ripples in a pond.
When those waves hit something big and hard, like a cliff or a wall, they bounce back to your ears.
Then why don't I hear an echo in my bedroom?
Your room is small, so the sound comes back super fast and mixes with your voice. In a big space, it takes longer, so you hear it again.
Soft things like pillows, curtains and soft toys soak up sound, so they make echoes quieter.
Yes! Bats make high squeaks and listen for the echoes. That helps them find their way and catch bugs in the dark.
Dolphins do it too, underwater! Using echoes like this is called echolocation.
So an echo is sound bouncing back off something big and hard!
That's right! Ask a grown-up to subscribe to The Curio Kids Club for more wonders! And next time someone asks... what is an echo?
